questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the 'No error' option.**

The equipment (A)/ in the lab don’t (B)/ work well. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'B'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the verb '**don’t**' is incorrect.
 
• The word '**equipment**' is a singular noun and requires a singular verb form.
 
• The correct verb form should be '**doesn't**' instead of 'don’t' to agree with the singular noun '**equipment**'.
 
• Therefore, the plural form of the verb '**don’t**' should be replaced with the singular form '**doesn't**'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: The equipment *in the lab doesn’t* work well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option A**: 'The equipment' – This part is correct as 'equipment' is a singular noun.
 
• **Option C**: 'work well' – This part is correct as it follows the subject-verb agreement rules.
 
• **Option D**: 'No error' – This option is incorrect because there is an error in part B.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. 

The teacher gave some useful advices to the students before the board exam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'advices to the students'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, **'advice to the students**' should be used instead of **'advices to the students'.**
 
• "**Advice**" is an **uncountable noun**, which means that it does not have** a plural form**. Even though it refers to a collection of ideas or suggestions, it is considered **a singular** **noun** in English **grammar**.
 
• In this sentence, "**advice**" is used as **an uncountable noun** to refer to a general concept or idea, rather than a specific set of suggestions.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The teacher gave some useful** __advice to the students__** before the board exam.*

questions.question:
**A phrase in the following sentence has been underlined. Choose the most appropriate phrase from the given alternatives to improve the sentence. Pick ‘No improvement’ in case no improvement is required.**

Could you pass __**a few sugar**__ to me?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"the sugar". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ‘Sugar’ is an uncountable noun and using ‘a’ or ‘few’ before it is meaningless and grammatically incorrect. 
 
• The alternative (3)** the sugar** is the only appropriate improvement for the given sentence. 
 
• The **‘the’ **before sugar signifies that it is at a definite position and is being referred to directly.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3". **

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the 'No error' option.**

Rahuls house is (P) / located in a peaceful residential area (Q) / in the beautiful city of Srinagar (R) / No error (S)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part P of the question. So, The correct answer is option 1.

In English, the Genitive form of a noun is used to show possession or ownership by using *‘s and s’* for people and other living beings. In order to understand the correct usage of ‘s and s, the following table is helpful :

 

 
 

 
 
 Type

 
 
 
Example

 
 
 
Genitive noun

 
 
 

 
 
Singular noun and name not ending in –s

 
 
 
Kamal, cat

 
 
 
Kamal’s umbrella, cat’s tail

 
 
 

 
 
Singular nouns ending in –s

 
 
 
Nicholas, actress

 
 
 
Nicholas’s car, Actress’s career

 
 
 

 
 
Plural noun

 
 
 
Boys, girls

 
 
 
Boys’ dinner, girls’ uniforms

 
 
 

 
 
Irregular plural noun (plurals that do not end in –s)

 
 
 
Children, men

 
 
 
Children’s books, men’s room

 
 
 

 

Here, the house being referred to belongs to Rahul. Rahul’s (and not Rahuls) will fit right into the sentence.

__Correct sentence__ – **Rahul’s** house is located in a peaceful residential area in the beautiful city of Srinagar.

questions.question:
**A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Four alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to 'No improvement'.**

I look forward to __meet you.__
questions.solution:
__
 
• The correct answer option is **"meeting you."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb **‘meet’ **should be in the gerund form (-ing form) after **‘look forward to’ **in a sentence.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be **‘I look forward to meeting you’. **

**Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 1". **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Gerunds **are verbs that have an **-ing **attached to it.
 
• The difference between a present participle that also has an -ing form attached to it and a gerund is that gerunds are verbs with -ing form that function as nouns.
 
 
• Example: **Reading books is my passion. **Here the word **reading **is the subject of the sentence that acts as a **noun** even though it is a verb (read) with an -ing form.
 
• Here, **reading **is a **gerund.** In the given question, **meeting **is not a verb, but a gerund; a verb with an -ing form acting as a noun.
